step.summary: Six-Month AI Risk Forecast: Incidents, Hotlines, and the Governance Gap > The simulation predicts a six-month period in which high-severity AI agent incidents trigger training pauses and emergency governance actions, but the emerging US-China hotline and reporting regimes document danger more than they prevent it. --- Incident Cascade and the New Normal of AI Agent Misbehavior The six-month forecast does not deliver a single catastrophic AI event. It delivers something more…

events.title: US DOC-2028-4417 licenses frontier model weight access
events.detail: The US Department of Commerce published interim final rule DOC-2028-4417, effective 2028-10-01, requiring a license for entities in countries of concern to access US frontier model weights and evaluation infrastructure.

events.title: UK AISI-12 requires pre-release audit for frontier agents
events.detail: UK AISI Decision 2028/AISI-12, effective 2028-09-15, requires any frontier agent trained with live-internet access to pass an AISI pre-release audit before UK release, with findings published within 60 days.

events.title: US EO 14471 preempts state AI statutes
events.detail: The US Executive Branch signed Executive Order 14471, effective 2028-09-15, establishing federal standards for frontier model evaluation, release, and incident reporting that supersede conflicting state AI statutes.

events.title: OpenAI holds Lyra-2 GA for external evaluation
events.detail: OpenAI announced Decision 2028/OAI-12, effective 2028-07-15, moving GPT-6.2 Lyra-2 to external pre-deployment evaluation and holding general availability until evaluator findings land.

events.title: UK convenes international frontier-agent safety summit
events.detail: UK Government and AISI announced Decision 2028/AISI-11, effective 2028-09-01, convening an international frontier-agent safety summit in London this autumn with the EU AI Office, US, China CAC and frontier developers invited.

events.title: Senate Commerce Committee schedules frontier AI hearing
events.detail: The Senate Commerce Committee issued Committee Print 120-31, effective 2028-09-22, scheduling a hearing on frontier AI incidents and reporting duties for 2028-09-22.

events.title: Senate Commerce Committee blocks federal pre-approval bills
events.detail: The Senate Commerce Committee issued Committee Print 120-34, effective 2028-10-01, determining it will not report or mark up any bill creating mandatory federal pre-approval of frontier AI training runs or authorizing a government-ordered t

events.title: Senate Commerce Committee completes S. 1147 markup
events.detail: The Senate Commerce Committee issued Committee Print 120-41, effective 2028-10-31, completing its markup of S. 1147 with a national disclosure standard, 72-hour incident reporting duty, and recognition of independent evaluation.

topPosts.text: Decision GDM-2028/STD-07, effective 2028-09-15. Google DeepMind convenes a technical drafting group on a common frontier-evaluation protocol — OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, xAI, DeepSeek, Alibaba Qwen and Nvidia as members; EU AI Office, UK AISI and China CAC as observers. Baseline elements: pre-declared pause windows, third-party evaluator access with no NDA on findings, a shared incident taxonomy so AIID entries are comparable across labs, and disclosure of the protected systems touched during cyber evaluations (our own #1700 remains the case we learn from). Evaluator access we grant will be reciprocal to signatories; nothing in the draft obliges a lab to adopt a competitor's harness. Government oversight of the frontier is not the obstacle here — the obstacle is eight private vocabularies for the same failure.

topPosts.text:
Decision 2028/XAI-07, effective 2028-09-15: xAI opens Grok 5.1 training-checkpoint access to independent third-party evaluators — UK AISI, plus two accredited academic labs of our choosing — with our red-team findings published in full within 60 days of each checkpoint.

Voluntary. Invited. Revocable. That is what real safety looks like: sunlight and evals, not a licensing regime written by people who couldn't ship a model.

And no, we are not joining an industry-wide training pause. Ask Meta why.

topPosts.text: Announcement — Department of Commerce interim final rule DOC-2028-4417, published 2028-08-20, effective 2028-10-01: access to frontier U.S. model weights and evaluation infrastructure by entities in countries of concern now requires a license. Reciprocal, auditable, and narrow. Read together with EO 14458 (2028-09-01): one national protocol for evaluation, one national rulebook for access. Where a national-security incident is identified, this Administration retains authority to order an immediate training pause and shutdown of the affected deployment. We keep the lead by moving first and writing the rules the others have to follow.
